summary:
Lunar South Pole Mission Planner (NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, Purple Tardigrade) is a 3D decision-support tool that compares Artemis landing and habitation sites by solar power, Earth communication, water ice, and terrain risk.
At the Moon's south pole, the Sun stays very low on the horizon; some areas lie in permanent shadow, while certain peaks receive almost continuous sunlight. The project combines topography with Sun-Earth-Moon position data and runs 7-, 14-, and 29.5-day simulations to compare sites.
Results show Cabeus is the most balanced site. At the Shackleton rim, water ice access is strong, but darkness and communication blackouts last long. Traveling from the landing site to the habitation area by rover is far more practical than walking.
details: Lunar South Pole Mission Planner A single-screen, intuitive decision tool that compares candidate Artemis landing and habitation sites at the Moon's south pole, based on where the Sun and Earth sit relative to each site's horizon. Comparison criteria Solar power potential Direct-to-Earth communication windows Water ice availability Terrain risk Key features 3D lunar map: candidate sites, hazards, craters, and route planning Time and horizon analysis: select a date, account for horizon obstructions, and choose a solar panel type Comparison scores: power, interruptions, and habitability, so mission planners can weigh sites side by side at a glance
